**Richard Milhous Nixon** (January 9, 1913–April 22, 1994) was the 37th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"), serving from 1969 until [his resignation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resignation_of_Richard_Nixon "Resignation of Richard Nixon") in 1974. A member of the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), he represented [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") in both houses of the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") before serving as the 36th [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") under President [Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Dwight D. Eisenhower") from 1953 to 1961. [His presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Richard_Nixon "Presidency of Richard Nixon") saw the reduction of U.S. involvement in the [Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War"), _[détente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%C3%A9tente "Détente")_ with the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China"), the [Apollo 11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11") Moon landing, and the establishment of the [Environmental Protection Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency") and [Occupational Safety and Health Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupational_Safety_and_Health_Administration "Occupational Safety and Health Administration"). Nixon's second term ended early when he became the only U.S. president to resign from office, as a result of the [Watergate scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watergate_scandal "Watergate scandal").

Nixon was born into a poor family of [Quakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quakers "Quakers") in [Yorba Linda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorba_Linda "Yorba Linda"), Southern California. He graduated from [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College") with a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in 1934 and from [Duke University School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_University_School_of_Law "Duke University School of Law") with a [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws") degree in 1937, practiced law in [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), and then moved with his wife [Pat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon") to [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), in 1942 to work for the [federal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_government_of_the_United_States "Federal government of the United States"). After serving in the [Naval Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Reserve "United States Navy Reserve") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), he was elected to the [House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") in [1946](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_California's_12th_congressional_district_election "1946 California's 12th congressional district election"). His work on the [Alger Hiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alger_Hiss "Alger Hiss") case established his reputation as a leading [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communism "Anti-communism"). In 1950, he [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_United_States_Senate_election_in_California "1950 United States Senate election in California") to the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). Nixon was the running mate of Eisenhower, the Republican Party's presidential nominee in the [1952](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election "1952 United States presidential election") and [1956 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_United_States_presidential_election "1956 United States presidential election"). Nixon served for eight years as vice president, and his two terms saw an increase in the notability of the office. He narrowly lost the [1960 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_United_States_presidential_election "1960 United States presidential election") to [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy"). After his loss in the [1962](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1962_California_gubernatorial_election "1962 California gubernatorial election") race for governor of California, Nixon announced his retirement from politics. However, he ran again for the presidency in [1968](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_United_States_presidential_election "1968 United States presidential election") and defeated the Democratic candidate, Vice President [Hubert Humphrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey "Hubert Humphrey").

Seeking to bring the North Vietnamese to the negotiating table, Nixon ordered [military operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambodian_campaign "Cambodian campaign") and [carpet bombing campaigns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Menu "Operation Menu") in Cambodia. He covertly aided Pakistan during the [Bangladesh Liberation War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bangladesh_Liberation_War "Bangladesh Liberation War") in 1971 and ended American combat involvement in Vietnam in 1973, and the [military draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States "Conscription in the United States") the same year. His [visit to China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_visit_by_Richard_Nixon_to_China "1972 visit by Richard Nixon to China") in 1972 led to [diplomatic relations between the two nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Communiqu%C3%A9_on_the_Establishment_of_Diplomatic_Relations "Joint Communiqué on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations"), and he finalized the [Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Ballistic_Missile_Treaty "Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty") with the Soviet Union. During the course of his first term, he enacted many progressive environmental policy shifts, such as creating the [Environmental Protection Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency") and passing laws, including the [Endangered Species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_Species_Act_of_1973 "Endangered Species Act of 1973") and [Clean Air Acts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Air_Act_(United_States) "Clean Air Act (United States)"). In addition to implementing the [Twenty-sixth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-sixth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-sixth Amendment to the United States Constitution") that lowered the voting age from 21 to 18, he ended the [direct international convertibility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bretton_Woods_system "Bretton Woods system") of the U.S. dollar to gold in 1971, effectively taking the United States off the [gold standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_standard "Gold standard"). He also imposed [wage and price controls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_Stabilization_Act_of_1970 "Economic Stabilization Act of 1970") for 90 days, launched the wars [on cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_cancer "War on cancer") and [drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_Drugs "War on Drugs"), passed the [Controlled Substances Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controlled_Substances_Act "Controlled Substances Act"), and presided over the end of the [Space Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Race "Space Race") by overseeing the Apollo 11 Moon landing. He was re-elected in [1972](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_United_States_presidential_election "1972 United States presidential election"), when he defeated [George McGovern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_McGovern "George McGovern") in [one of the largest landslide victories in American history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_presidential_elections_by_popular_vote_margin "List of United States presidential elections by popular vote margin").

In his second term, Nixon ordered [an airlift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Nickel_Grass "Operation Nickel Grass") to resupply Israeli materiel losses in the [Yom Kippur War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War "Yom Kippur War"), a conflict which led to the [oil crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1973_oil_crisis "1973 oil crisis") at home. From 1973, ongoing revelations from the Nixon administration's involvement in Watergate eroded his support in Congress and the country. The scandal began with a break-in at the [Democratic National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_National_Committee "Democratic National Committee") office, ordered by administration officials, and escalated despite [cover-up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cover-up "Cover-up") efforts by the Nixon administration, of which he was aware. On August 9, 1974, facing almost certain [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_process_against_Richard_Nixon "Impeachment process against Richard Nixon") and removal from office, Nixon resigned. Afterward, he was issued [a controversial pardon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardon_of_Richard_Nixon "Pardon of Richard Nixon") by his successor, [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford"). During nearly 20 years of retirement, Nixon wrote nine books and undertook many foreign trips, rehabilitating his image into that of an elder statesman and leading expert on foreign affairs. On April 18, 1994, he suffered a debilitating [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke "Stroke") and [died four days later](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_and_state_funeral_of_Richard_Nixon "Death and state funeral of Richard Nixon").

## Early life and education

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a7/Nixon_child.jpeg/250px-Nixon_child.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nixon_child.jpeg)

Nixon (second from right) makes his newspaper debut in 1916, contributing five cents to a fund for [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I") orphans; his brother [Donald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Nixon "Donald Nixon") is to his right.

Richard Milhous Nixon was born on January 9, 1913, in what was then the township precinct of [Yorba Linda, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorba_Linda,_California "Yorba Linda, California"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-1) in a house built by his father, on his family's lemon ranch.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-archives-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENPS,_Nixon_Birthplace-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFerris209-4) His parents were [Francis A. Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_A._Nixon "Francis A. Nixon") and [Hannah (Milhous) Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Milhous_Nixon "Hannah Milhous Nixon"). His mother was a [Quaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quaker "Quaker"), and his father converted from [Methodism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Methodism "Methodism") to the Quaker faith. Through his mother, Nixon was a descendant of the early English settler Thomas Cornell.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-5)

Nixon's upbringing was influenced by Quaker observances of the time, such as abstinence from alcohol, dancing, and swearing. He had four brothers: Harold, [Donald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Nixon "Donald Nixon"), Arthur, and [Edward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Nixon "Edward Nixon").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Childhood-6) Four of the five Nixon boys were named after British kings; Richard was named after [Richard the Lionheart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_I_of_England "Richard I of England").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken11-7)

Nixon's early life was marked by hardship, and he later quoted [Dwight Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Eisenhower "Dwight Eisenhower") in describing his boyhood: "We were poor, but the glory of it was we didn't know it".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken12-8) The Nixon family ranch failed in 1922, and the family moved to [Whittier, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier,_California "Whittier, California"). In an area of East Whittier with many Quakers, Frank Nixon opened a grocery store and gas station at what is now the corner of Whittier Boulevard and Santa Gertrudes Avenue.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken21-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-10) During this period, the Nixon family attended East Whittier Friends Church.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-11) Richard's younger brother Arthur died in 1925 at the age of seven after a short illness.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose198741-12) Richard was 12 years old when a spot was found on his lung; with a family history of [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis"), he was forbidden to play sports. The spot turned out to be scar tissue from [pneumonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pneumonia "Pneumonia").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken27-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose198756%E2%80%9357-14)

### Primary and secondary education

[![Image 11](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2c/Richard_Nixon_HS_Yearbook.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Richard_Nixon_HS_Yearbook.jpg)

Nixon as a senior at [Whittier High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_High_School "Whittier High School") in 1930

Nixon attended East Whittier Elementary School, where he was president of his eighth-grade class.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack16-15) His older brother Harold had attended [Whittier High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_High_School "Whittier High School"), which his parents thought resulted in a dissolute lifestyle. They decided to send Nixon to the larger [Fullerton Union High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fullerton_Union_High_School "Fullerton Union High School").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris89-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack17%E2%80%9319-17) Though he had to ride a school bus an hour each way during his freshman year, he attained excellent grades. Later, he lived with an aunt in [Fullerton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fullerton,_California "Fullerton, California") during the week.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris91-18) He played junior varsity football and seldom missed practice, though he rarely was used in games.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris92-19) He had greater success as a debater, winning several championships and taking his only formal tutelage in public speaking from Fullerton's Head of English, H. Lynn Sheller. Nixon later mused on Sheller's words, "Remember, speaking is conversation...don't shout at people. Talk to them. Converse with them."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken28-20) Nixon said he tried to use a conversational tone as much as possible.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken28-20)

At the start of his junior year in September 1928, Nixon's parents permitted him to transfer to Whittier High School. At Whittier, Nixon lost a bid for student body president—his first electoral defeat. He often rose at 4 a.m. to drive the family truck to Los Angeles to purchase vegetables and then drove to the store to wash and display them before going to school. Harold was diagnosed with tuberculosis the previous year; when their mother took him to Arizona, hoping to improve his health, the demands on Nixon increased, causing him to give up football. Nevertheless, Nixon graduated from Whittier High third in his class of 207.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack20%E2%80%9323-21)

### College and law school

Nixon was offered a tuition grant to attend [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"), but with Harold's continued illness requiring his mother's care until he died in 1933, Richard was needed at the store. He remained in his hometown and enrolled at [Whittier College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittier_College "Whittier College") in September 1930. His expenses were met by his maternal grandfather.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-archives-2)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack23%E2%80%9324-22) Nixon played for the basketball team; he also tried out for football, and though he lacked the size to play, he remained on the team as a substitute and was noted for his enthusiasm.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman15-23) Instead of fraternities and sororities, Whittier had literary societies. Nixon was snubbed by the only one for men, the Franklins, many of whom were from prominent families, unlike Nixon. He responded by helping to found a new society, the Orthogonian Society.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack24%E2%80%9325-24) In addition to the society, his studies, and work at the store, Nixon engaged in several extracurricular activities; he was a champion debater and hard worker.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose198761-25) In 1933, he was engaged to Ola Florence Welch, daughter of the Whittier police chief, but they broke up in 1935.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken58%E2%80%9363-26)

After graduating _[summa cum laude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin\_honors#North\_America "Latin honors")_ with a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") in history from Whittier in 1934, Nixon was accepted at the new [Duke University School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_University_School_of_Law "Duke University School of Law"),[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Student_&_Sailor-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-28) which offered scholarships to top students, including Nixon.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose198733%E2%80%9334-29) It paid high salaries to its professors, many of whom had national or international reputations.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken67-30) The number of scholarships was greatly reduced for second- and third-year students, creating intense competition.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose198733%E2%80%9334-29) Nixon kept his scholarship, was elected president of the Duke Bar Association,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParmet81-31) inducted into the [Order of the Coif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_Coif "Order of the Coif"),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Family_Collection_Guide-32) and graduated third in his class with a [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws") degree in June 1937.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Student_&_Sailor-27)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENaval_Historical_Center,_Commander_Nixon-34)

## Early career and marriage

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/Formal_Nixon_Family_Portrait_with_Julie_and_David_Eisenhower%3B_President_Richard_Nixon%2C_First_Lady_Pat_Nixon%2C_Tricia_and_Edward_Cox_-_DPLA_-_4cdb5ada26f5bc179a46bc005a4d523f.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Formal_Nixon_Family_Portrait.jpg)

Nixon's family: [Julie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Nixon_Eisenhower "Julie Nixon Eisenhower") and [David Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Eisenhower "David Eisenhower"), President Nixon, First Lady [Pat Nixon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon"), [Tricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricia_Nixon_Cox "Tricia Nixon Cox"), and [Edward Cox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_F._Cox "Edward F. Cox") on December 24, 1971

After graduating from Duke, Nixon initially hoped to join the [FBI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Bureau_of_Investigation "Federal Bureau of Investigation"). He received no response to his application and learned years later that he had been hired, but his appointment had been canceled at the last minute due to budget cuts.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken76-35) He was admitted to the [California bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Bar_of_California "State Bar of California") in 1937, and began practicing in Whittier with the law firm Wingert and Bewley in the [National Bank of Whittier Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bank_of_Whittier_Building "National Bank of Whittier Building").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Student_&_Sailor-27)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-36) His work concentrated on [commercial litigation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_law "Commercial law") for local petroleum companies and other corporate matters, as well as on [wills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_(law) "Will (law)").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken79%E2%80%9382-37) Nixon was reluctant to work on divorce cases, disliking frank sexual talk from women.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris193-38) In 1938, he opened up his own branch of Wingert and Bewley in [La Habra, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Habra,_California "La Habra, California"),[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack44-39) and became a full partner in the firm the following year.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack43-40) In later years, Nixon proudly said he was the only modern president to have previously worked as a practicing attorney.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris193-38) During this period, Nixon was also the president of the Citra-Frost Company, which attempted to produce and sell frozen orange juice, but the company went bankrupt after 18 months.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-NixonsCounty-41)

In January 1938, Nixon was cast in the Whittier Community Players production of _[The Dark Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Tower\_(play) "The Dark Tower (play)")_ in which he played opposite his future wife, a high school teacher named [Thelma "Pat" Ryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Nixon "Pat Nixon").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Student_&_Sailor-27) In his memoirs, Nixon described it as "a case of [love at first sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love_at_first_sight "Love at first sight")",[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon197823-42) but apparently for Nixon only, since Pat Ryan turned him down several times before agreeing to date him.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFarrell385%E2%80%93393-43) Once they began their courtship, Ryan was reluctant to marry Nixon; they dated for two years before she assented to his proposal. They wed in a small ceremony on June 21, 1940. After a honeymoon in [Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexico "Mexico"), the Nixons began their married life in Whittier.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFarrell37,_402-44) They had two daughters: [Tricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricia_Nixon_Cox "Tricia Nixon Cox"), born in 1946, and [Julie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Nixon_Eisenhower "Julie Nixon Eisenhower"), born in 1948.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Nixon_Family-45)

## Military service

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Formal_portrait_of_Lt._Commander_Richard_Nixon_wearing_a_coat_and_Navy_hat_-_NARA_-_16916087.jpg/250px-Formal_portrait_of_Lt._Commander_Richard_Nixon_wearing_a_coat_and_Navy_hat_-_NARA_-_16916087.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Formal_portrait_of_Lt._Commander_Richard_Nixon_wearing_a_coat_and_Navy_hat_-_NARA_-_16916087.jpg)

Nixon as a lieutenant commander in the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy"), c.1945

In January 1942, the couple moved to the Northern Virginia suburbs, where Nixon took a job at the [Office of Price Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Office_of_Price_Administration "Office of Price Administration") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Student_&_Sailor-27)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon197826-46) In his political campaigns, Nixon suggested that this was his response to [Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor"), but he had sought the position throughout the latter part of 1941. Both Nixon and his wife believed he was limiting his prospects by remaining in Whittier.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris124%E2%80%93126-47) He was assigned to the tire rationing division, where he was tasked with replying to correspondence. He did not enjoy the role, and four months later applied to join the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKornitzer143%E2%80%93144-48) Though he could have claimed an exemption from [the draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscription_in_the_United_States "Conscription in the United States") as a birthright Quaker, or a deferral due to his government service, Nixon nevertheless sought a commission in the Navy. His application was approved, and he was appointed a [lieutenant junior grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_(junior_grade) "Lieutenant (junior grade)") in the [United States Naval Reserve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy_Reserve "United States Navy Reserve") on June 15, 1942.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken96%E2%80%9397-50)

In October 1942, he was given his first assignment as aide to the commander of the [Naval Air Station Ottumwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottumwa_Regional_Airport#History "Ottumwa Regional Airport") in [Wapello County, Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wapello_County,_Iowa "Wapello County, Iowa"), until May 1943. Seeking more excitement, he requested sea duty; on July 2, 1943, he was assigned to [Marine Aircraft Group 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Aircraft_Group_25 "Marine Aircraft Group 25") and the [South Pacific Combat Air Transport Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Pacific_Combat_Air_Transport_Command "South Pacific Combat Air Transport Command") (SCAT), where he supported the [logistics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_logistics "Military logistics") of operations in the [South Pacific theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean_theater_of_World_War_II "Pacific Ocean theater of World War II") during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENaval_Historical_Center,_Commander_Nixon-34)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack58%E2%80%9360-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmstrong81-52)

On October 1, 1943, Nixon was promoted to [lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_(navy) "Lieutenant (navy)").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49) Nixon commanded the SCAT forward detachments at [Vella Lavella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vella_Lavella "Vella Lavella"), [Bougainville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buin,_Papua_New_Guinea#Japan_and_the_USA_during_World_War_II "Buin, Papua New Guinea"), and finally at [Nissan Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nissan_Island "Nissan Island").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEArmstrong81-52) His unit prepared manifests and flight plans for [R4D/C-47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Douglas_C-47_Skytrain "Douglas C-47 Skytrain") operations and supervised the loading and unloading of the transport aircraft. For this service, he received a [Navy Letter of Commendation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commendation_Medal "Commendation Medal") and a Navy Commendation Ribbon, which was later updated to the [Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_and_Marine_Corps_Commendation_Medal "Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medal"), from his commanding officer for "meritorious and efficient performance of duty as Officer in Charge of the South Pacific Combat Air Transport Command". Upon his return to the U.S., Nixon was appointed the administrative officer of the [Alameda Naval Air Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Alameda "Naval Air Station Alameda") in [Alameda, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alameda,_California "Alameda, California"). In January 1945, he was transferred to the [Bureau of Aeronautics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Aeronautics "Bureau of Aeronautics") office in [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), where he helped negotiate the termination of World War II contracts, and received his second letter of commendation, from the [Secretary of the Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_the_Navy "United States Secretary of the Navy")[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack62-53) for "meritorious service, tireless effort, and devotion to duty". Later, Nixon was transferred to other offices to work on contracts, and he moved to Philadelphia, New York, and finally to Baltimore.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken112-54)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon197833-55) On October 3, 1945, he was promoted to [lieutenant commander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_commander_(United_States) "Lieutenant commander (United States)").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack62-53) On March 10, 1946, he was relieved of active duty.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49) On June 1, 1953, he was promoted to [commander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander_(United_States) "Commander (United States)") in the U.S. Naval Reserve, and he retired from the U.S. Naval Reserve on June 6, 1966.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-navy.mil-49)

While in the Navy, Nixon became a very good [five-card stud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-card_stud "Five-card stud") poker player, helping finance his first congressional campaign with the winnings. In a 1983 interview, he described turning down an invitation to dine with [Charles Lindbergh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Lindbergh "Charles Lindbergh") because he was hosting a game.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-57)

## U.S. House of Representatives (1947–1950)

Further information: [1946 California's 12th congressional district election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1946_California's_12th_congressional_district_election "1946 California's 12th congressional district election") and [1948 California's 12th congressional district election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_California's_12th_congressional_district_election "1948 California's 12th congressional district election")

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Nixonflyer1946.jpg/250px-Nixonflyer1946.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nixonflyer1946.jpg)

Nixon's 1946 congressional campaign flyer

Republicans in [California's 12th congressional district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California's_12th_congressional_district "California's 12th congressional district") were frustrated by their inability to defeat Democratic representative [Jerry Voorhis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Voorhis "Jerry Voorhis"), and they sought a consensus candidate who would run a strong campaign against him. In 1945, they formed a "Committee of 100" to decide on a candidate, hoping to avoid internal dissensions which had led to previous Voorhis victories. After the committee failed to attract higher-profile candidates, Herman Perry, manager of Whittier's [Bank of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America "Bank of America") branch, suggested Nixon, a family friend with whom he had served on Whittier College's board of trustees before the war. Perry wrote to Nixon in [Baltimore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore "Baltimore"), and after a night of excited conversation with his wife, Nixon gave Perry an enthusiastic response,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParmet91%E2%80%9396-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman27%E2%80%9328-59) confirming that he was registered to vote in California at his parents' Whittier residence.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken114-60) Nixon flew to California and was selected by the committee. When he left the Navy at the start of 1946, Nixon and his wife returned to Whittier, where he began a year of intensive campaigning.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParmet91%E2%80%9396-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman27%E2%80%9328-59) He contended that Voorhis had been ineffective as a representative and suggested that Voorhis's endorsement by a group linked to Communists meant that Voorhis must have radical views.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParmet111%E2%80%93113-61) Nixon won the election, receiving 65,586 votes to Voorhis's 49,994.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman82-62)

In June 1947, Nixon supported the [Taft–Hartley Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft%E2%80%93Hartley_Act "Taft–Hartley Act"), a federal law that monitors the activities and power of labor unions, and he served on the [Education and Labor Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_Committee_on_Education_and_Labor "United States House Committee on Education and Labor"). In August 1947, he became one of 19 House members to serve on the [Herter Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herter_Committee "Herter Committee"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-Final-63) which went to Europe to report on the need for U.S. foreign aid. Nixon was the youngest member of the committee and the only Westerner.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman105%E2%80%93107,_125%E2%80%93126-64) Advocacy by Herter Committee members, including Nixon, led to congressional passage of the [Marshall Plan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Plan "Marshall Plan").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris365-65)

In his memoirs, Nixon wrote that he joined the [House Un-American Activities Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Un-American_Activities_Committee "House Un-American Activities Committee") (HUAC) "at the end of 1947". However, he was already a HUAC member in early February 1947, when he heard "Enemy Number One" [Gerhard Eisler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerhard_Eisler "Gerhard Eisler") and his sister [Ruth Fischer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_Fischer "Ruth Fischer") testify. On February 18, 1947, Nixon referred to Eisler's belligerence toward HUAC in his maiden speech to the House. Also by early February 1947, fellow U.S. Representative [Charles J. Kersten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_J._Kersten "Charles J. Kersten") had introduced him to Father [John Francis Cronin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Francis_Cronin "John Francis Cronin") in Baltimore. Cronin shared with Nixon his 1945 privately circulated paper "The Problem of American Communism in 1945",[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-66) with much information from the FBI's [William C. Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_C._Sullivan "William C. Sullivan") who by 1961 headed domestic intelligence under [J. Edgar Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Edgar_Hoover "J. Edgar Hoover").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-NixonV1-67) By May 1948, Nixon had co-sponsored the [Mundt–Nixon Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mundt%E2%80%93Nixon_Bill "Mundt–Nixon Bill") to implement "a new approach to the complicated problem of internal communist subversion... It provided for registration of all [Communist Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CPUSA "CPUSA") members and required a statement of the source of all printed and broadcast material issued by organizations that were found to be Communist fronts." He served as floor manager for the Republican Party. On May 19, 1948, the bill passed the House by 319 to 58, but later it failed to pass the Senate.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon1978Running_for_Congress:_1946-68) The Nixon Library cites this bill's passage as Nixon's first significant victory in Congress.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-69)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Congressman_Richard_Nixon%2C_Yorba_Linda%2C_circa_April_1950_%285494854338%29.jpg/250px-Congressman_Richard_Nixon%2C_Yorba_Linda%2C_circa_April_1950_%285494854338%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Congressman_Richard_Nixon,_Yorba_Linda,_circa_April_1950_(5494854338).jpg)

Nixon in [Yorba Linda, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yorba_Linda,_California "Yorba Linda, California"), c.April 1950

Nixon first gained national attention in August 1948, when his persistence as a House Un-American Activities Committee member helped break the [Alger Hiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alger_Hiss "Alger Hiss") spy case. While many doubted [Whittaker Chambers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whittaker_Chambers "Whittaker Chambers")'s allegations that Hiss, a former [State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_State "United States Department of State") official, had been a [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") spy, Nixon believed them to be true and pressed for the committee to continue its investigation. After Hiss filed suit, alleging defamation, Chambers produced documents corroborating his allegations, including paper and [microfilm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microfilm "Microfilm") copies that Chambers turned over to House investigators after hiding them overnight in a field; they became known as the "[Pumpkin Papers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pumpkin_papers "Pumpkin papers")".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack129%E2%80%93135-70) Hiss was convicted of [perjury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perjury "Perjury") in 1950 for denying under oath he had passed documents to Chambers.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman239%E2%80%93241-71) In [1948](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_California's_12th_congressional_district_election "1948 California's 12th congressional district election"), Nixon successfully [cross-filed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross-filed "Cross-filed") as a candidate in his district, winning both major party primaries,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris381-72) and was comfortably reelected.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Congressman-73)

## U.S. Senate (1950–1953)

See also: [1950 United States Senate election in California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1950_United_States_Senate_election_in_California "1950 United States Senate election in California")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Nixon_handout_1950.jpg/250px-Nixon_handout_1950.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nixon_handout_1950.jpg)

Nixon's 1950 Senate campaign flyer

In 1949, Nixon began to consider running for the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") against the conservative Democratic incumbent, [Sheridan Downey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheridan_Downey "Sheridan Downey"),[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman282-74) and entered the race in November.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris535-75) Downey, faced with a bitter primary battle with Representative [Helen Gahagan Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Gahagan_Douglas "Helen Gahagan Douglas"), announced his retirement in March 1950.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman296%E2%80%93297-76) Nixon and Douglas won the primary elections[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman304-77) and engaged in a contentious campaign in which the ongoing [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War") was a major issue.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman310-78) Nixon tried to focus attention on Douglas's liberal voting record. As part of that effort, a "[Pink Sheet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_election_in_California,_1950#Debut_of_the_Pink_Sheet "United States Senate election in California, 1950")" was distributed by the Nixon campaign suggesting that Douglas's voting record was similar to that of New York Congressman [Vito Marcantonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vito_Marcantonio "Vito Marcantonio"), reputed to be a communist, and their political views must be nearly identical.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris581-79) Nixon won the election by almost twenty percentage points.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman335-80) During the campaign, Nixon was first called "Tricky Dick" by his opponents for his campaign tactics.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman303-81) After Nixon won, Downey resigned effective November 30, 1950; this enabled the governor to appoint Nixon on December 1, giving him a seniority advantage over other senators elected in 1950, whose terms started in January 1951.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-82)

In the Senate, Nixon took a prominent position in opposing global [communism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Communism "Communism"), traveling frequently and speaking out against it.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Senator-83) He maintained friendly relations with [Joseph McCarthy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McCarthy "Joseph McCarthy"), a controversial U.S. Senate colleague from [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin") and fellow [anti-communist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-communism "Anti-communism"), but was careful to keep some distance between himself and McCarthy's allegations.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987211,_311%E2%80%93312-84) Nixon criticized President Harry S. Truman's handling of the [Korean War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_War "Korean War").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTENixon_Library,_Senator-83) He supported statehood for [Alaska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska "Alaska") and [Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii"), voted in favor of civil rights for minorities, and supported federal disaster relief for [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") and [Yugoslavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack178-85) He voted against price controls and other monetary restrictions, benefits for illegal immigrants, and public power.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack178-85)

## Vice presidency (1953–1961)

See also: [Presidency of Dwight D. Eisenhower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Dwight_D._Eisenhower "Presidency of Dwight D. Eisenhower")

Further information: [Checkers speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkers_speech "Checkers speech")

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Richard_Nixon_Vice_Presidential_Portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Richard_Nixon_Vice_Presidential_Portrait_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Richard_Nixon_Vice_Presidential_Portrait_(cropped).jpg)

Nixon's official portrait as [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States"), c.1953–1961

Nixon's speech at a state Republican Party fundraiser in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") on May 8, 1952, impressed Governor [Thomas E. Dewey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_E._Dewey "Thomas E. Dewey"), who was an Eisenhower supporter and had organized a pro-Eisenhower delegation from New York to attend the [national convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_Republican_National_Convention "1952 Republican National Convention").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman418-86) In a private meeting following the speech, Dewey suggested to Nixon that he would make a suitable vice presidential candidate to run alongside Eisenhower.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman418%E2%80%93419-87) Eisenhower later indicated to Paul H. Davis of the [Hoover Institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoover_Institution "Hoover Institution") at [Stanford University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University "Stanford University"), an intermediary between candidates Eisenhower and [Earl Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earl_Warren "Earl Warren"), that if he won the nomination, Nixon would be his first choice for the vice presidency, because Eisenhower believed the party needed to promote leaders who were aggressive, capable, and young.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGellman433-434-88) Eisenhower later developed a list of seven potential candidates, with Nixon's name at the top.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose262-89)

After Eisenhower was nominated, his key supporters met to discuss vice presidential possibilities.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose262-89) Eisenhower informed the group's chairman, [Herbert Brownell Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_Brownell_Jr. "Herbert Brownell Jr.") that he did not wish to appear to dictate to the convention by formally sponsoring a single candidate, so the group reviewed several, including [Robert A. Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_A._Taft "Robert A. Taft"), [Everett Dirksen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everett_Dirksen "Everett Dirksen"), and [Alfred E. Driscoll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_E._Driscoll "Alfred E. Driscoll"), all of whom they quickly rejected.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose262-89) Dewey then raised Nixon's name; the group quickly concurred.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose262%E2%80%93263-90) Brownell checked with Eisenhower, who indicated his approval.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose263-91) Brownell then called Nixon to inform him that he was Eisenhower's choice.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose262%E2%80%93263-90) Nixon accepted, then departed for Eisenhower's hotel room to discuss the details of the campaign and Eisenhower's plans for his vice president if the ticket was successful in the [general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election "1952 United States presidential election").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose263-91)

The delegates soon assembled to formalize the selection.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose264-92) Nixon asked Senator [William Knowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Knowland "William Knowland") to nominate him, and Knowland agreed.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose264-92) After Senator [John W. Bricker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_W._Bricker "John W. Bricker"), who had supported Taft for president, declined Nixon's request to second the nomination, Driscoll agreed to do so.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose264%E2%80%93265-93) There were no other candidates, and Nixon was nominated by acclamation.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose265-94)

On the campaign trail, Eisenhower spoke of his plans for the country, and left the negative campaigning to his [running mate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_mate "Running mate").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken222%E2%80%93223-95) In mid-September, the Republican ticket faced a major crisis when the media reported that Nixon had a political fund, maintained by his backers, which reimbursed him for political expenses.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKornitzer191-97) Such a fund was not illegal, but it exposed Nixon to allegations of a potential conflict of interest. With pressure building for Eisenhower to demand Nixon's resignation from the [ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticket_(politics) "Ticket (politics)"), Nixon went on television to address the nation on September 23, 1952.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken210%E2%80%93217-98) The address, later named the [Checkers speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Checkers_speech "Checkers speech"), was heard by about 60 million Americans, which represented the largest audience ever for a television broadcast at that point.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThompson291-99) In the speech, Nixon emotionally defended himself, stating that the fund was not secret and that his donors had not received special favors. He painted himself as a patriot and man of modest means, mentioning that his wife had no mink coat; instead, he said, she wore a "respectable Republican cloth coat".[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken210%E2%80%93217-98) The speech was remembered for the gift which Nixon had received, but which he would not give back, which he described as "a little cocker spaniel dog...sent all the way from Texas. And our little girl—Tricia, the 6-year-old—named it Checkers."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken210%E2%80%93217-98) The speech prompted a huge public outpouring of support for Nixon.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken218-100) Eisenhower decided to retain him on the ticket,[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris846-101) and the ticket was victorious in [the November election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1952_United_States_presidential_election "1952 United States presidential election").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken222%E2%80%93223-95)

Eisenhower granted Nixon more responsibilities during his term than any previous vice president.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-102) Nixon attended [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Cabinet "United States Cabinet") and [National Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Security_Council_(USA) "National Security Council (USA)") meetings and chaired them in Eisenhower's absence. A 1953 tour of the Far East succeeded in increasing local goodwill toward the United States and gave Nixon an appreciation of the region as a potential industrial center. He visited [Saigon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ho_Chi_Minh_City "Ho Chi Minh City") and [Hanoi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanoi "Hanoi") in [French Indochina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Indochina "French Indochina").[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken225%E2%80%93227-103) On his return to the United States at the end of 1953, Nixon increased the time he devoted to foreign relations.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987342-104)

Biographer Irwin Gellman, who chronicled Nixon's congressional years, said of his vice presidency:

> Eisenhower radically altered the role of his running mate by presenting him with critical assignments in both foreign and domestic affairs once he assumed his office. The vice president welcomed the president's initiatives and worked energetically to accomplish White House objectives. Because of the collaboration between these two leaders, Nixon deserves the title, "the first modern vice president".[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-Gellman-Small-105)

Despite intense campaigning by Nixon, who reprised his strong attacks on the Democrats, the Republicans lost control of both houses of Congress in the [1954 elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_United_States_elections "1954 United States elections"). These losses caused Nixon to contemplate leaving politics once he had served out his term.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987357%E2%80%93358-106) On September 24, 1955, President Eisenhower suffered a heart attack, and his condition was initially believed to be life-threatening. Eisenhower was unable to perform his duties for six weeks. The [Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-fifth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution") had not yet been proposed, and the vice president had no formal power to act. Nonetheless, Nixon acted in Eisenhower's stead during this period, presiding over Cabinet meetings and ensuring that aides and Cabinet officers did not seek power.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken256%E2%80%93258-107) According to Nixon biographer [Stephen Ambrose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Ambrose "Stephen Ambrose"), Nixon had "earned the high praise he received for his conduct during the crisis... he made no attempt to seize power".[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987375%E2%80%93376-108)

His spirits buoyed, Nixon sought a second term, but some of Eisenhower's aides aimed to displace him. In a December 1955 meeting, Eisenhower proposed that Nixon not run for reelection and instead become a Cabinet officer in a second Eisenhower administration, to give him administrative experience before a 1960 presidential run. Nixon believed this would destroy his political career. When Eisenhower announced his reelection bid in February 1956, he hedged on the choice of his running mate, saying it was improper to address that question until he had been renominated. Although no Republican was opposing Eisenhower, Nixon received a substantial number of write-in votes against the president in the 1956 [New Hampshire primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Hampshire_primary "New Hampshire primary") election. In late April, the President announced that Nixon would again be his running mate.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAitken237%E2%80%93241-109) Eisenhower and Nixon were reelected by a comfortable margin in the [November 1956 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1956_United_States_presidential_election "1956 United States presidential election").[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEParmet294-110)

In early 1957, Nixon undertook another foreign trip, this time to Africa. On his return, he helped shepherd the [Civil Rights Act of 1957](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Act_of_1957 "Civil Rights Act of 1957") through Congress. The bill was weakened in the Senate, and civil rights leaders were divided over whether Eisenhower should sign it. Nixon advised the President to sign the bill, which he did.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack349%E2%80%93352-111) Eisenhower suffered a mild [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke "Stroke") in November 1957, and Nixon gave a press conference, assuring the nation that the Cabinet was functioning well as a team during Eisenhower's brief illness.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBlack355-112)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c2/Kitchen_debate.jpg/250px-Kitchen_debate.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kitchen_debate.jpg)

[Nikita Khrushchev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev "Nikita Khrushchev") and Nixon speak as the press looks on at the [Kitchen Debate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_Debate "Kitchen Debate") on July 24, 1959; _[What's My Line?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/What's\_My\_Line%3F "What's My Line?")_ host [John Charles Daly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Charles_Daly "John Charles Daly") is on the far left.

On April 27, 1958, Richard and Pat Nixon reluctantly embarked on a goodwill tour of [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America"). In [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo"), Uruguay, Nixon made an impromptu visit to a college campus, where he fielded questions from students on U.S. foreign policy. The trip was uneventful until the Nixon party reached [Lima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima"), Peru, where he was met with student demonstrations. Nixon went to the historical campus of [National University of San Marcos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_University_of_San_Marcos "National University of San Marcos"), the oldest university in the Americas, got out of his car to confront the students, and stayed until forced back into the car by a volley of thrown objects. At his hotel, Nixon faced another mob, and one demonstrator spat on him.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987465%E2%80%93469-113) In [Caracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracas "Caracas"), Venezuela, Nixon and his wife were spat on by anti-American demonstrators and [their limousine was attacked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Richard_Nixon's_motorcade "Attack on Richard Nixon's motorcade") by a pipe-wielding mob.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987469%E2%80%93479-114) According to Ambrose, Nixon's courageous conduct "caused even some of his bitterest enemies to give him some grudging respect".[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAmbrose1987463-115) Reporting to the cabinet after the trip, Nixon claimed there was "absolute proof that [the protestors] were directed and controlled by a central Communist conspiracy." Secretary of State [John Foster Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Foster_Dulles "John Foster Dulles") and his brother, [Director of Central Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_Central_Intelligence "Director of Central Intelligence")[Allen Dulles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allen_Dulles "Allen Dulles"), both concurred with Nixon.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-116)

In July 1959, Eisenhower sent Nixon to the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") for the opening of the [American National Exhibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_National_Exhibition "American National Exhibition") in Moscow. On July 24, Nixon was touring the exhibits with [Nikita Khrushchev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev "Nikita Khrushchev") when the two stopped at a model of an American kitchen and engaged in an impromptu exchange about the merits of capitalism versus communism that became known as the "[Kitchen Debate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kitchen_Debate "Kitchen Debate")".[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFarrell1394%E2%80%931400-117)
